name: Spare Office
replaces: Microsoft 365: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, OneNote, OneDrive and Forms
summary: Documents, spreadsheets, slides, mail and calendar, chat and meetings, notes, forms and file storage in one suite that is free to use and owned by its members. Files save in open formats, Microsoft's formats are read and written from their published standards, and people, scripts and AI agents all use the same commands.

areas.name: Getting started: accounts, organisations and home
areas.summary: Signing up once, landing on a home screen that shows your work, and setting up a household, club, school or business with its own people and web address.

features.name: Sign up and sign in
features.does: Create one Spareware login and use it for every Spare Office app on every device.

parts.name: Kit sign-in in Spare Office
parts.what: Uses the kit's passkeys, password fallback and second sign-in step, and lets an organisation require the second step for its members.

parts.name: Switch between accounts
parts.what: Keep a personal and a work account signed in side by side, and switch with one click. Every app has people with both, so this belongs in the kit's accounts.

features.name: First-run welcome
features.does: Pick a language, region and look on first use, and get offered a move-in from another suite.

parts.name: Welcome flow
parts.what: Language, region, paper size, theme and accessibility choices asked once and remembered.

parts.name: Starter files
parts.what: A short sample document, sheet and deck that teach the basics by using them.

parts.name: Bring your stuff prompt
parts.what: Offers to bring across mail, files and calendars from another suite, linking to the move-in hub.

features.name: Home screen and app launcher
features.does: Open recent and pinned files, see what was shared with you, and jump between the eight apps.

parts.name: Home screen
parts.what: Recent, pinned and shared-with-me files across all apps, with quick search.

parts.name: App launcher and switcher
parts.what: One menu to move between Write, Sheets, Slides, Mail, Chat, Notes, Drive and Forms.

parts.name: Create new from anywhere
parts.what: A New button that makes any kind of file from a blank page or a template.

features.name: Profile and settings
features.does: Set your name, photo, pronouns, time zone and working hours once for every app.

parts.name: Working profile
parts.what: Adds time zone, working hours and work location to the kit's profile, with who can see each set by the person.

parts.name: Settings that follow you
parts.what: Personal settings saved as operations so they reach every device.

features.name: Set up an organisation
features.does: Create a workspace for a business, school, club or iwi group, invite people and give them roles.

parts.name: Office organisations on the kit's model
parts.what: Uses the kit's one organisation model and adds Office's organisation types (business, school, club, iwi group, household) and their settings.

parts.name: Invites and join requests
parts.what: Invite by email or link, approve join requests, and set what new members get, using the kit's team invites.

parts.name: Roles and permissions
parts.what: Office's owner, admin, member and guest roles, plus custom roles for larger groups, defined on the kit's roles.

parts.name: Groups
parts.what: Groups of people that can own files, receive mail and join channels together, kept in the kit's organisation model.

parts.name: Protected organisation names
parts.what: Checks new organisation names and logos against government agencies, banks and other well-known bodies, and holds lookalikes for a person to review.

features.name: Use your own web address
features.does: Prove you own a domain and use it for your organisation's email and sign-in.

parts.name: Domain verification
parts.what: Checks a DNS record to prove ownership of a domain before it is used. Spare Market shops and Spare Social handles need the same check, so it belongs in the kit.

parts.name: DNS set-up helper
parts.what: Shows the exact records to add, checks them live, and explains each in plain words.

features.name: Households and small groups
features.does: Share storage, a calendar and a family folder with the people you live with.

parts.name: Household group
parts.what: A small organisation type with a shared calendar, shared folder and shared storage allowance.

features.name: Guests and people outside
features.does: Let someone without an account view or edit a file, fill a form or join a meeting.

parts.name: Guest access
parts.what: One-time code by email gives a guest access to just what was shared with them.

parts.name: Guest limits and expiry
parts.what: Guest access ends on a set date and can be removed in one place.

parts.name: Guests in chat
parts.what: Guests can join chosen team channels and chats, clearly labelled as guests, with limits on what they can see, start and share.

features.name: Accounts for children and schools
features.does: Schools give students managed accounts with safe defaults, and parents can see what applies.

parts.name: School-managed accounts
parts.what: Accounts created and controlled by a school, with chat, sharing and mail limits set by the school.

parts.name: End-of-year rollover
parts.what: Moves students up a year, closes leavers' accounts after an export offer, and sets up new classes in one run.

features.name: Help and support
features.does: Find plain-language help inside any app, and reach the kit's support and member forum from there.

parts.name: Office help articles
parts.what: Short how-to pages for every Spare Office feature, in plain words and translated, published in the kit's help centre.

parts.name: Help inside the apps
parts.what: Search help from any screen, with the answer shown next to the work.

features.name: Show your organisation is real
features.does: Get a verified badge on your organisation once its NZ Business Number is checked.

parts.name: Verified organisation badge
parts.what: Shows a badge on an organisation's sign-in page, invites, forms and booking pages once the kit's business number lookup confirms it.

features.name: Get a web address
features.does: Buy a web address for your organisation during set-up, at cost, from an authorised registrar.

parts.name: Registrar choice
parts.what: Which authorised .nz registrars offer a reseller interface and terms that let the co-op pass on their price at cost.

parts.name: Domain purchase at cost
parts.what: Buys a domain through the chosen registrar at its price, then adds the mail and sign-in records for the organisation.

areas.name: Shared document core
areas.summary: One core under Write, Sheets, Slides and Notes: styled text, tables, pictures, shapes, charts, maths, spelling, clipboard, printing and templates, built once so every app behaves the same.

features.name: Write and format text
features.does: Type, select and format text with fonts, sizes, colours, highlighting, spacing and alignment.

parts.name: Document model
parts.what: Blocks, paragraphs, runs and objects with permanent IDs, shared by every editor; whether to partner, reuse or build decides its starting point.

parts.name: Document commands
parts.what: Every document edit (insert, delete, format, move) described once as a command schema on the kit's operations, so undo, co-editing, scripts and AI share one path.

parts.name: Paragraph layout
parts.what: Text shaping, line breaking, hyphenation and justification through the shared text engine.

parts.name: Editing surface
parts.what: Cursor, selection, keyboard and input-method handling for every script, drawn on a canvas with an accessible mirror.

features.name: Styles and themes
features.does: Apply named paragraph and character styles, and a theme of fonts and colours that every app shares.

parts.name: Style sheets
parts.what: Named styles with inheritance, so changing one style updates every use of it.

parts.name: Shared themes
parts.what: Theme fonts, colours and effects defined once and used by Write, Sheets and Slides.

parts.name: Style gallery
parts.what: Pick, preview, change and create styles from a panel.

features.name: Tables
features.does: Insert tables, merge and split cells, set borders and shading, and repeat header rows.

parts.name: Table model and layout
parts.what: Rows, columns, merged cells and auto-fit widths laid out with the text engine.

parts.name: Table tools
parts.what: Insert, delete, resize, sort and style tables from the keyboard or a menu.

features.name: Pictures, shapes and diagrams
features.does: Insert pictures, crop them, wrap text around them, and draw shapes, text boxes, arrows and simple diagrams.

parts.name: Picture handling
parts.what: Insert, crop, rotate, compress and set text wrap for pictures, keeping the original for later edits.

parts.name: Shapes and connectors
parts.what: Our own set of shapes, lines and connectors that stay joined when moved.

parts.name: Diagrams from lists
parts.what: Turn a bullet list into a process, cycle, hierarchy or org chart drawn with our own designs.

parts.name: Open icon and picture library
parts.what: Icons and stock pictures that are our own work or openly licensed, with each licence recorded.

features.name: Charts
features.does: Make a chart from data and place it in a sheet, document or slide.

parts.name: Chart engine
parts.what: Bar, line, pie, area, scatter, combo, histogram, waterfall, box and map charts drawn from a data range.

parts.name: Chart editor
parts.what: Pick a chart type, switch rows and columns, and edit titles, axes, labels and colours.

parts.name: Chart format mapping
parts.what: Read and write chart parts in OpenDocument and Office Open XML files.

parts.name: Chart text alternatives
parts.what: Every chart carries a short description and an optional data table that screen readers can read, kept in both file formats.

features.name: Maths and equations
features.does: Write equations by typing maths shorthand or picking symbols, and see them typeset.

parts.name: Equation engine
parts.what: Lays out equations from a linear input such as LaTeX or UnicodeMath, using an open maths font.

parts.name: Equation formats
parts.what: Reads and writes MathML for OpenDocument and Office Math Markup for Word files.

features.name: Pen and freehand drawing
features.does: Draw and write with a pen, finger or mouse on documents, slides and notes.

parts.name: Ink engine
parts.what: Pressure-sensitive strokes with smoothing, erasing and highlighting, stored as operations.

parts.name: Ink formats
parts.what: Saves ink in OpenDocument drawing form and reads and writes Office ink markup.

parts.name: Keep slideshow ink
parts.what: Offers to keep the pen marks made during a show as ink on the slides, saved in both file formats.

features.name: Find, replace and move around
features.does: Find and replace text, formatting and special characters, and jump by heading, page or comment.

parts.name: Find and replace
parts.what: Plain, match-case, whole-word, wildcard and pattern search with replace across the file.

parts.name: Navigation pane
parts.what: Outline of headings, pages and objects to jump to and drag to reorder.

features.name: Spelling, grammar and words
features.does: Get spelling and grammar suggestions, look up synonyms and count words as you write.

parts.name: Spell checker
parts.what: Checks spelling against open dictionaries in many languages while typing.

parts.name: Grammar and style checker
parts.what: Flags grammar, clarity and wordiness with reasons, using an engine whose licence suits the core.

parts.name: Thesaurus and word count
parts.what: Synonyms on right-click and live counts of words, characters and reading time.

parts.name: Language marking
parts.what: Set the language of a paragraph or phrase, or let it be detected, so spelling, grammar, hyphenation and read-aloud switch between English and te reo Māori in one document.

features.name: Undo, copy and paste
features.does: Undo and redo anything, and copy and paste between apps and from other programs with formatting kept.

parts.name: Rich clipboard
parts.what: Copies in our own format plus HTML, RTF, plain text and pictures, and cleans pasted web content.

parts.name: Paste options
parts.what: Keep formatting, match formatting or paste plain text, chosen after pasting.

features.name: Print and page set-up
features.does: Print or save as PDF with paper size, margins and orientation, seeing a preview first.

parts.name: Print preview
parts.what: Shows pages exactly as they will print, page by page.

parts.name: Page set-up
parts.what: Paper sizes with A4 as the NZ default, margins, orientation and printer choice.

features.name: Templates
features.does: Start from a template, save your own, and use your organisation's shared templates.

parts.name: Template format and store
parts.what: Templates kept as normal files with fill-in fields, listed in a gallery.

parts.name: Starter template set
parts.what: Letters, CVs, invoices with GST, budgets, timesheets, minutes and decks, made by us for NZ first.

parts.name: Organisation templates
parts.what: Admins publish branded templates that members see first.

features.name: Live pieces shared between files
features.does: Paste a table, chart or list into another file and keep it updated everywhere it appears.

parts.name: Live embeds
parts.what: A shared piece with one source that updates in every document, deck, note and chat it is placed in.

parts.name: Embeds in Office files
parts.what: When saved to Office or OpenDocument files, a live piece becomes a normal copy with a link back.

features.name: Links and bookmarks
features.does: Link text to web pages, places in the same file, other files or email addresses.

parts.name: Hyperlinks and bookmarks
parts.what: Links and named places that survive saving to every supported format.

parts.name: Link previews
parts.what: Shows the title of a linked Spare file, or of a web page through the kit's tracking-free link previews, on hover.

features.name: Type faster
features.does: Have quotes, lists and capitals fixed as you type, insert symbols, and reuse saved blocks of text.

parts.name: AutoCorrect and format as you type
parts.what: Smart quotes, automatic lists, capitals at the start of sentences and common typo fixes, with a list per language that each person can change.

parts.name: Insert symbol
parts.what: A searchable picker for symbols and special characters, including macron vowels, with recent ones first.

parts.name: Saved text blocks
parts.what: Save a block of text, a table or a signature once and insert it anywhere, for yourself or shared by an organisation.

areas.name: File formats and fidelity
areas.summary: Saving in OpenDocument, and opening and saving Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF and other files faithfully, all from published standards so nobody is locked in and nothing breaks the legal rules.

features.name: Save in OpenDocument
features.does: Save documents, sheets, slides and drawings as OpenDocument 1.4 files (.odt, .ods, .odp and .odg) that any OpenDocument app can open.

parts.name: Format standards research
parts.what: OpenDocument (ISO/IEC 26300) and Office Open XML (ECMA-376, ISO/IEC 29500): the specs and the hardest parts to get right; patent promises are checked once, in the format patent check.

parts.name: OpenDocument reader and writer
parts.what: Reads and writes OpenDocument 1.4 text, spreadsheet, presentation and drawing files, and reads older versions, to and from the document model.

parts.name: OpenDocument conformance tests
parts.what: Round-trip and validator tests against the published schema and openly licensed sample files.

features.name: Open and save Word files
features.does: Open a .docx, edit it, and send it back so it looks the same in Word.

parts.name: Office Open XML package
parts.what: Shared reader and writer for the zip package, relationships, themes and shared parts of every Office Open XML file.

parts.name: Word document reader and writer
parts.what: Maps WordprocessingML paragraphs, styles, numbering, sections, fields and tracked changes to the document model and back.

parts.name: Layout fidelity corpus
parts.what: A set of openly licensed real-world documents with expected page layouts, used to measure how faithfully each file lays out.

parts.name: Legal and print page features
parts.what: Watermarks, page borders, line numbers, drop caps, linked text boxes and tables of authorities laid out and kept on save, even before Write has tools to make them.

parts.name: Templates, shows and macro-enabled files
parts.what: Opens and saves templates (.dotx, .xltx, .potx), slide shows (.ppsx) and macro-enabled files (.docm, .xlsm, .pptm), which use the same package with other content types. Macros never run.

parts.name: Office Open XML Strict
parts.what: Reads and writes the Strict form of ISO/IEC 29500 as well as the Transitional form most files use.

features.name: Open and save Excel files
features.does: Open a .xlsx with its formulas, formats, charts and pivot tables, and save it back intact.

parts.name: Excel workbook reader and writer
parts.what: Maps SpreadsheetML cells, shared strings, styles, formulas, names, tables and pivot caches to the sheet model and back.

parts.name: Formula translation
parts.what: Converts between Office Open XML formulas and OpenFormula so formulas survive either format.

features.name: Open and save PowerPoint files
features.does: Open a .pptx with its masters, layouts, animations and media, and save it back intact.

parts.name: PowerPoint reader and writer
parts.what: Maps PresentationML slides, masters, layouts, shapes, transitions and animations to the slide model and back.

parts.name: Drawing markup mapping
parts.what: Shared DrawingML shapes, fills, effects and text frames used by Word, Excel and PowerPoint files.

features.name: Open older Office files
features.does: Open .doc, .xls and .ppt files from before 2007 and save them in a current format.

parts.name: Binary format readers
parts.what: Readers for the old Word, Excel and PowerPoint binary formats built only from Microsoft's published Open Specifications.

features.name: Save and print to PDF
features.does: Save any file as a PDF that keeps links, headings and alt text, or as an archival PDF.

parts.name: PDF export
parts.what: Exports pages through the shared PDF engine with links, bookmarks and embedded fonts.

parts.name: Tagged and archival PDF
parts.what: Uses engine-pdf's tagged (PDF/UA) and archival (PDF/A) output, passing it headings, reading order, table headers and alt text. The output belongs in engine-pdf so Spare Studio shares it.

features.name: Turn a PDF into an editable file
features.does: Open a PDF and get an editable document with its text, tables and pictures.

parts.name: PDF to document conversion
parts.what: Turns PDF pages into an editable document with engine-pdf's PDF-to-editable conversion, shared with Spare Studio, and maps the result to the document model.

features.name: Other everyday formats
features.does: Open and save CSV, plain text, RTF, Markdown, HTML and EPUB.

parts.name: CSV and TSV
parts.what: Reads and writes delimited text with encoding, separator and date-format detection.

parts.name: RTF reader and writer
parts.what: Rich Text Format from Microsoft's published specification, for older programs and the clipboard.

parts.name: Markdown and HTML
parts.what: Import and export Markdown and clean HTML, keeping headings, lists, tables and links.

parts.name: EPUB export
parts.what: Exports long documents as accessible e-books.

features.name: Fonts that match
features.does: Open files that use fonts you don't have and still keep the same line and page breaks.

parts.name: Open font bundle
parts.what: Open-licence fonts for every script, including metric-compatible fonts for common Office fonts, with licences recorded.

parts.name: Font substitution table
parts.what: Maps each common font name to a metric-compatible open font so layouts don't shift.

parts.name: Font embedding
parts.what: Embeds and reads embedded fonts in documents where the font's licence allows it.

parts.name: A match for Aptos
parts.what: Find an openly licensed font with the same widths as Aptos, Office's current default font, so recent files don't reflow. Akasia (OFL) claims this; check its licence, how its widths were made and how well it matches before bundling it.

features.name: Files with macros
features.does: Open files that contain macros safely, keep the macros on save, and know what they would do.

parts.name: Macro keeping
parts.what: Keeps macro parts untouched when a file is saved again, without running them.

parts.name: Macro warning
parts.what: Tells the person a file has macros and that they are not run.

parts.name: Macro language research
parts.what: Whether a macro interpreter built from Microsoft's published language spec is lawful and worth the effort, versus converting to our scripts.

features.name: Compatibility check
features.does: Before saving to a Microsoft format, see anything that won't come through the same.

parts.name: Round-trip loss checker
parts.what: Lists features in the file that the target format can't hold, with where they are.

features.name: Repair damaged files
features.does: Open a damaged or partly corrupt file and recover as much as possible.

parts.name: Tolerant readers
parts.what: Readers that skip broken parts, report what was lost and never crash on bad input.

parts.name: Format fuzzing
parts.what: Continuous fuzz testing of every reader, seeded with the hostile file set, so bad files can't crash or harm the app.

features.name: Password-protected files
features.does: Open and save password-protected OpenDocument and Office files.

parts.name: File encryption
parts.what: Reads and writes file encryption from the published OpenDocument and Office encryption specifications.

features.name: Open files safely
features.does: Open any file knowing it can't fetch things from the internet or run anything without asking.

parts.name: Active content policy
parts.what: On open, never fetches remote templates, linked pictures or outside data, and never runs DDE fields, OLE objects, data connections or macros.

parts.name: Ask before refreshing links
parts.what: Asks before refreshing links to other workbooks, outside data or linked pictures, showing where each link points.

parts.name: Hostile file tests
parts.what: A set of files built to fetch or run things, such as remote-template and DDE files, tested against every reader on every change.

features.name: Open Excel binary workbooks and saved Outlook messages
features.does: Open and save .xlsb workbooks, and open .msg files saved or dragged from Outlook.

parts.name: .xlsb reader and writer
parts.what: Reads and writes Excel binary workbooks from Microsoft's published MS-XLSB specification.

parts.name: .msg reader
parts.what: Reads saved Outlook messages from Microsoft's published MS-OXMSG specification, into Mail or as a file preview.

features.name: Keep embedded objects
features.does: Open files with embedded objects, such as a table inside a document, see them, and keep them when saving.

parts.name: Embedded object previews
parts.what: Shows the stored picture of each embedded object and keeps the object unchanged on save. Objects are never run.

parts.name: Open embedded files
parts.what: Opens an embedded spreadsheet or document as its own file in the matching Spare app, when its format is one we read.

features.name: Open Visio diagrams
features.does: Open .vsdx diagrams to view and print them.

parts.name: Diagram format clearance
parts.what: An owner confirms the patent promise and terms that cover Microsoft's published MS-VSDX specification before code is written.

parts.name: Diagram reader
parts.what: Reads .vsdx drawings from the MS-VSDX specification into the drawing model, for viewing and printing.

features.name: Bring Access data across
features.does: Bring tables and data from Access database files into Lists or Sheets.

parts.name: Database scope decision
parts.what: Whether Spare Office needs a database app, or only a lawful way to bring Access data across using a published specification or an owner-cleared method. Many small businesses and schools run on Access files.

features.name: Rescue old Publisher files
features.does: Open years of old Publisher newsletters and flyers, if a lawful way exists.

parts.name: Publisher rescue decision
parts.what: Microsoft stopped offering Publisher in Microsoft 365 in October 2026. An owner decides whether Spare Studio or Spare Office takes this on, and whether any lawful way to read .pub files exists.

areas.name: Co-editing, comments, history and offline
areas.summary: Working on the same file at the same time, talking about it in comments, suggesting changes, going back to any earlier version, and carrying on with no connection, all without ever losing work.

features.name: Edit together live
features.does: See other people's cursors and edits appear as they type, in documents, sheets, slides and notes.

parts.name: Co-editing design
parts.what: How co-editing runs on the kit operation log, with a text CRDT where the log alone isn't enough, and how no work is ever lost.

parts.name: Rich-text merging
parts.what: Builds on the kit's text CRDT to merge concurrent formatting, tables and objects, so everyone ends with the same document.

parts.name: Sheet co-editing
parts.what: Cell, row and column operations that merge cleanly, with recalculation order kept the same for everyone.

parts.name: Slide and canvas co-editing
parts.what: Merges moves, resizes and edits to shapes on slides, whiteboards and note pages.

parts.name: Presence in files
parts.what: Shows who is in a file, where their cursor is and what they have selected, on the kit's presence. Agents show as labelled co-editors with the person they act for.

features.name: Comments and mentions
features.does: Comment on any part of a file, reply, resolve, and mention someone so they are told.

parts.name: Comment threads
parts.what: Threads anchored to text, cells, shapes or slides that stay attached as the file changes.

parts.name: Mentions
parts.what: Mentioning a person notifies them and offers to share the file if they can't open it yet.

parts.name: Comment pane
parts.what: Read, filter, reply to and resolve comments, and reply from an email notification.

parts.name: Comment formats
parts.what: Comments and replies kept when saving to OpenDocument and Office files.

features.name: Suggest and track changes
features.does: Suggest edits instead of making them, then accept or reject each one.

parts.name: Tracked change model
parts.what: Insertions, deletions, moves and format changes recorded per person and saved as standard revision marks.

parts.name: Review pane
parts.what: Step through changes, accept or reject one or all, and filter by person.

parts.name: Compare two files
parts.what: Shows the differences between two versions of a document as tracked changes.

features.name: Version history
features.does: See every earlier version, who changed what, name a version and restore it.

parts.name: Named versions and restore
parts.what: Name important versions and restore or copy any version without losing later ones.

parts.name: Show changes by person
parts.what: Colours each part of the file by who last changed it and when.

features.name: Work offline
features.does: Open and edit files with no connection, and have everything merge when back online.

parts.name: Offline file cache
parts.what: Keeps chosen and recent files on the device, ready to open with no connection.

parts.name: Merge after offline work
parts.what: Merges a long offline session into the live file, showing anything that needs a person to choose.

features.name: Never lose work
features.does: Have every change saved as you go, and get it back after a crash or a flat battery.

parts.name: Continuous save
parts.what: Every operation saved to the local journal and the server; there is no save button to forget.

parts.name: Crash recovery
parts.what: Replays the local journal after a crash so the file opens exactly where it was.

parts.name: Save a copy
parts.what: Save a copy to a chosen place and format whenever wanted.

features.name: Lock or finalise a file
features.does: Reserve a file for yourself while you edit it, or mark it final so it isn't changed by accident.

parts.name: Check-out and final marks
parts.what: Exclusive edit locks with expiry, and a final mark that asks before any edit.

features.name: Work with people on other suites
features.does: Send and receive Office files, and share a link that opens in any browser for people without Spare Office.

parts.name: Office files in shared folders
parts.what: Office files in Drive stay in their format when edited, so people using other suites can keep working on them.

parts.name: Open-in-browser links
parts.what: A share link opens the file in the browser editor with no install and no account needed to view.

features.name: Get deleted items back
features.does: Restore a deleted email, event, contact, note page, plan card or chat message for a set time, even after the bin was emptied.

parts.name: Recoverable mail, calendar and contacts
parts.what: Keeps items for a set time after the mail, calendar or contacts bin is emptied, on the kit's recycle bin, and restores a whole meeting series at once.

parts.name: Recoverable notes and chat
parts.what: The same restore for note pages, sections and chat messages, and for plan cards once plan boards arrive.

parts.name: Recover deleted items view
parts.what: One place in each app to see recently deleted items and put them back.

areas.name: Spare Write: documents
areas.summary: Everything a word processor needs on top of the shared core: pages, sections, lists, long documents, references, mail merge, protection, signing and dictation.

features.name: Lay out pages
features.does: Set margins, columns, sections, page breaks, headers, footers and page numbers.

parts.name: Pagination engine
parts.what: Breaks the document into pages with widow and orphan control, keep-with-next and floating objects.

parts.name: Sections and columns
parts.what: Sections with their own page size, orientation, margins and columns.

parts.name: Headers, footers and page numbers
parts.what: Different first page, odd and even pages, and page number formats per section.

parts.name: Page layout view
parts.what: Edit directly on the pages as they will print, with rulers and margins.

features.name: Lists and numbering
features.does: Make bullet and numbered lists, including multi-level legal numbering that restarts and continues correctly.

parts.name: Multi-level list engine
parts.what: List definitions, levels, restart and continue rules that match both file formats.

features.name: Long documents
features.does: Build a table of contents, captions, cross-references, footnotes, endnotes and an index.

parts.name: Fields engine
parts.what: Page numbers, dates, cross-references, document properties and tables of contents that update themselves.

parts.name: Footnotes and endnotes
parts.what: Notes laid out at the foot of the page or the end, with numbering per section.

parts.name: Captions, index and table of figures
parts.what: Numbered captions, a marked index and lists of figures and tables.

parts.name: Outline view
parts.what: Work on the document as an outline of headings, moving whole sections at once.

features.name: Citations and bibliography
features.does: Add sources as you write and get a bibliography in APA, MLA, Chicago or another style.

parts.name: Citation style engine
parts.what: Formats citations from openly published citation style files, with a licence check on the engine used.

parts.name: Personal reference library
parts.what: Store sources once and cite them in any document.

features.name: Spare editors inside other websites

features.name: Use it in any browser

features.name: Phone and tablet apps

features.name: Print from anywhere

assess: Walk through a normal working day (read mail on a phone, join a meeting, edit a shared sheet with others, fill a form, find an old file): does every step land on a core feature, including the phone-sized browser layouts and web push, or is something missing?
Are the core features truly the smallest set for a first usable release? Does piece OF07 (first app: Write, Sheets or Mail) change which core features must come first?
Partner or build (piece OF01): which parts would ArtCraft's office apps or LibreOffice's engine already cover, and how much of the document core and file formats does that remove?
File fidelity: how will we prove files look the same in Word, Excel and PowerPoint using only published standards and openly licensed test files, never by reverse-engineering Microsoft's software?
Co-editing (pieces OF03 and A05): is the operation log plus a text CRDT enough to promise no lost work, including after days offline?

Mail: should the co-op run its own mail service at launch, given deliverability work, MTA-STS and DMARC on every hosted domain, quarantine and spam abuse, or start as an app for existing mail providers?

Chat and meetings (piece OF05): the kit now owns the one chat server and call service; is Matrix or our own protocol right for them, and are AGPL servers acceptable as separate services under our licence rules?
Which parts carry real running costs (storage, mail, meeting servers, speech recognition, AI), and what free allowance can members afford to vote for?

AI: does the demo make it clear the assistant is off until turned on, the person and their organisation pick the provider, content never trains a model, and an agent must ask a person before it sends mail, shares outside or deletes?
Accessibility: can canvas-drawn editors really work with every screen reader? Is the accessible mirror part sized and scheduled early enough?

Te reo Māori: who are our language and data-sovereignty partners for the interface, dictionaries, macron autocorrect, sorting, maramataka, speech models and voices, and are they involved from the start?

Legal: which legal parts need a lawyer before launch (privacy and IPP 3A, health information, telecommunications interception duties, harmful digital communications, illegal content, recording consent, electronic signatures, booking payments, overseas tax, import terms, Exchange protocol clearance)?

Scope edges: do video editing, diagramming, project scheduling, intranet sites, rosters, a video library, dashboards, low-code apps, Access databases and Publisher files belong in Spare Office, in Spare Studio or Spare Work, or later?
Moving in: do Microsoft's and Google's API terms allow our import tools, and what happens to chat history that can't be exported?
Are the part sizes believable? Which large parts should become new work-board pieces next?

Public sector and schools: do we target NZ government agencies and schools early (Public Records Act, the NZ Information Security Manual, Secure Government Email, classification labels, class notebooks, assignments and LTI) or later?
Does the demo use only our own names, look and icons, with Microsoft's product names appearing only to say what each app replaces?

Headless: does the demo show one task done by a person, a script and an agent through the same commands, with every Office app's command schemas in the command API and MCP server from the first release?
Safe files: does the demo open hostile test files (remote templates, DDE fields, macros, booby-trapped zips) without fetching or running anything, and serve every upload from a separate domain?
Leaving: can an admin take a whole organisation out in open formats and close it, can a person's export include version history and comments, and can a suspended person still export and appeal?

Kit dependencies: Office's first release needs the kit's regular payments, business accounts and desktop sync client to be core, and several parts say they belong in the kit or engines (speech, text recognition, domain checks, account switching, the organisation audit log, link checks, the separate file domain, the form engine). Have the kit and engines taken them on?
